issue_context.title: modem: HL7800: does not work with IPv6
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
If `CONFIG_NET_IPV6=y` and `CONFIG_NET_IPV4=n` the HL7800 driver will not work with IPv6 addresses.

**To Reproduce**
Modify `proj.conf` in this sample to test:
https://github.com/LairdCP/Pinnacle_100_Sample_Applications/tree/master/apps/low_power

**Expected behavior**
HL7800 driver should work with IPv4 only, IPv6 only, or both enabled.

**Impact**
Showstopper for those wanting to use IPv6 with the HL7800

review_comments:
I remembered that open braces should be the last char in a line?
```c
static const char *const dns_servers_str[] = {
        ictx.dns_v4_string,
        ...
```
nit: True, would be good to move the initialized to a new line.
This file was auto-formatted with the .clang-format file using VSCode. So I am going to leave this as is.

Personally from my limited experience I'd prefer
```c
#if IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_*)
```

rather than `#ifdef *` or `#if defined(*)` because `IS_ENABLED` is only true when the CONFIG_* is defined to 1 ~~, and the code will compile as intended if the user unintentionally or unknowingly defined `CONFIG_*` = false somewhere and expect the features to be disabled.~~

~~Please correct me if I'm wrong~~

EDIT: I'm wrong, see comments below.

Using `IS_ENABLED` is a good habit, but in practice there should be no big difference if one uses `defined`. I recall that there is a check that makes sure user is not able to define `CONFIG_` options in source files. Also one cannot define `CONFIG_*=false` in prj.conf file because Kconfig will make sure that the boolean value needs to be integer.

@jukkar Wouldn't `CONFIG_SOMETHING=n` in `prj.conf` or `someboard_defconfig` get compiled into `autoconf.h` as
```c
#define CONFIG_SOMETHING 0
```
, and `#ifdef CONFIG_SOMETHING` will then becomes true?

Dunno, but you can certainly try and see what happens. We do not have that many invocations of `#if IS_ENABLED()` in the source files atm, so it does not seem be a big concern right now.
`find . -name '*.[ch]' | xargs grep '#if IS_ENABLED'`

I checked my app's `autoconf.h` and found that configs that are specifically "n" defined in my `prj.conf` aren't being compiled, which is great and `#ifdef`/`#if defined` will do the job. I'm just too paranoid.
Thanks for the discussion. Going to leave this as is.
